frontier.hypothesis: Target's copy destination has a SECOND reader whose bytes are removed after register allocation by jump2's cross-jump (jump.c:1950-2061, runs after reload), merged into the shared return-0 tail .L800178AC.
frontier.mechanism: cross-jump deletes one of two identical post-RA instruction sequences that reach the same label; a reader of a3 inside a loop-body return arm would survive flow/combine (second use) and could disappear only if its allocated bytes equal the shared tail, which is j .L80017A1C ; addu v0,zero,zero and reads no register.
frontier.next_probe: Scratch TU on the m8 geometry with a real return-arm statement reading b in each loop body, then read .jump2 (cross-jump) and .dbr; on the chassis measure one such arm in loop 2 with sandbox and diff with s39/dis.sh. Expected outcome: class kill citing jump.c:1950ff (the merged tail cannot contain an a3 read), to be banked by dump rather than by reading.

frontier.hypothesis: A family grant covering a construct that can place a use-once register copy at a join-successor preheader without paying for its own address expression would re-open the residual; no such family is on the frozen list today.
frontier.mechanism: s37/s38/s39 prove combine's deletion, the block-boundary escape, the interposer escape and the reload producer are context-free; only a sanctioned construct with a second byte-free reader could change the pass input.
frontier.next_probe: On a future grant_rescan.py --apply hit, re-measure the BASE chassis with the newly granted construct spelling loop 2's preheader copy, then diff copy position against target with tmp/grind/func_80017848/s39/dis.sh.

frontier.hypothesis: An SOTN-master (PSX / GCC 2.7.2) precedent exhibiting the copy-then-redefine-source preheader idiom in a non-nested-loop context would convert the s18 decomp.me twin (scratch 19TpT) into a citable precedent and re-open gate (b).
frontier.mechanism: Gate (b) requires an in-hand SOTN-master file:line or commit; the present census over docs/reference/sotn-construct-index.md is negative.
frontier.next_probe: Re-run the construct-index census after any index regeneration, filtering PSX-tagged entries for a preheader reg-reg copy whose source is redefined by the very next add.
